reason: Allows an application to manage role assignments for any enterprise application in the tenant, potentially enabling an attacker to grant themselves other high-privileged roles.
Grants the ability to elevate privileges to the Global Administrator role or manage other directory roles, a significant security risk.
Allows an application to read and write data across the entire Azure Active Directory (Azure AD/Entra ID), including managing group memberships, which could lead to unauthorized access to resources.
Permits full read and write access to all user profiles, including the ability to reset passwords and modify sensitive properties.
Enables an attacker to modify the credentials of a more privileged application, allowing impersonation and potential access up to the Global Administrator level.
Allows an attacker to enable powerful authentication methods like the Temporary Access Pass (TAP) tenant-wide, facilitating user account takeover.
Grants extensive control over all SharePoint site collections, allowing for full data access or modification.
Grants extensive control over all SharePoint site collections, allowing for full data access or modification.
Allows an attacker to add a trusted root certificate to Entra ID and authenticate as any user, including a Global Administrator.
Allows creating active directory role assignments through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), so any principal, including the application itself, can be made a Global Administrator.
Allows making any principal eligible for any directory role through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), including Global Administrator; the principal can then activate the role.
Allows managing membership and ownership of groups through PIM for Groups, including role-assignable groups that hold privileged directory roles.
Allows adding active members or owners to groups through PIM for Groups, including role-assignable groups that hold privileged directory roles.
Allows making any principal an eligible member or owner of a group through PIM for Groups, including role-assignable groups that hold privileged directory roles.
Allows registering a new authentication method, such as a Temporary Access Pass or a phone number, for any user, enabling takeover of accounts including administrators.
Allows resetting users' passwords, enabling takeover of their accounts.
Allows adding a federated domain or changing a domain's federation settings, so an attacker-controlled identity provider can sign in as any user of that domain, including a Global Administrator.

Allows changing the membership and ownership of any group that is not role-assignable, granting whatever those groups confer, such as Azure roles, application access or exclusion from conditional access policies.
Allows changing the membership of any group that is not role-assignable, granting whatever those groups confer, such as Azure roles, application access or exclusion from conditional access policies.
Allows granting any delegated permission to any application on behalf of all users, so high-privilege delegated access can be consented to without an administrator.
Allows changing the tenant's consent policies, for example so that users can consent to high-privilege permissions without administrator approval.
Allows creating access packages and assigning them to any principal, which grants the group memberships, application roles and SharePoint site access the packages contain.
Allows changing Exchange Online role assignments, so a principal can be granted Exchange administrative roles, including ones that give access to mailboxes.
Allows deploying configuration and scripts to Intune-managed devices, which can run code with system privileges on them, including administrator workstations.
Allows creating and assigning Intune scripts, which run code with system privileges on managed devices, including administrator workstations.
Allows deploying applications to Intune-managed devices, which can install and run attacker-controlled software on them.
Allows changing Intune role assignments, so a principal can be given administrative control over managed devices.
Allows reading the local administrator passwords that Windows LAPS backs up to Entra ID, giving administrator access to those devices.
Allows changing, disabling or deleting conditional access policies, removing controls such as MFA and device compliance requirements.
Allows turning off security defaults, removing the baseline MFA requirements in tenants that rely on them.
Allows changing the tenant's authorization policy, which sets what ordinary users and guests may do, such as registering applications or consenting to them.
Allows changing Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role settings, such as removing the approval, MFA or justification required to activate a privileged directory role.
Allows changing PIM for Groups settings, such as removing the approval, MFA or justification required to activate membership of a privileged group.

Allows changing cross-tenant access settings, such as opening inbound access or trusting MFA and device claims from another tenant, which can create a lasting way in from a tenant an attacker controls.
Allows adding or changing the identity providers used for external identities, so accounts from an attacker-controlled provider can sign in.
Allows sending mail as any user in the tenant, which can be used for phishing or fraud that appears to come from a trusted colleague.
Allows reading the mail in every mailbox in the tenant.
Allows reading, changing and deleting the mail in every mailbox in the tenant.
Allows changing any user's mailbox settings, including creating inbox rules that forward or hide mail without the user noticing.
Allows reading every file in OneDrive and SharePoint across the tenant.
Allows reading, changing and deleting every file in OneDrive and SharePoint across the tenant.
Allows reading the documents and list items in every SharePoint site collection.
Allows creating, editing and deleting items and lists in every SharePoint site collection.
Allows reading every Teams chat message in the tenant.
Allows reading every Teams channel message in the tenant.
Allows creating eDiscovery cases and searches and exporting their results, which can collect mail, chats and files from across the tenant.
Allows reading the BitLocker recovery keys of all devices, which unlock a device's disk for anyone who holds the device or a copy of the disk.
Allows remote actions on Intune-managed devices, such as wiping them or resetting their passcodes.
